 Texas vs LSU injury report: Four players left to watch heading into Saturday 
 Here's the latest on Hero Kanu as the Texas Longhorns prepare to play the LSU Tigers. 
 David Eckert 0 
 AUSTIN, Texas — Amid the chaos brought by a nationwide ground stop, preventing all flights — including the one scheduled to take the Texas Longhorns to Baton Rouge — from taking off, we've still got an injury report to talk about. 
 There's no change for the Longhorns or the Tigers. Texas DL Hero Kanu is probable, while OL Cole Hutson is questionable. For LSU, linebacker Whit Weeks is questionable, while OL Weston Davis is probable. 
 (Photo: Getty) Hutson was not named in the report on Wednesday, but appeared Thursday. 
 Beyond Hutson and Kanu, there's not much to report on the Longhorn end of things. 
 Trevor Goosby, the Longhorns' star left tackle and likely a future first-round pick, is out for the season and listed as such. Running back Hollywood Smothers is also out. Like Goosby, he's not expected to return this season. 
 The same is true for Nick Townsend, a sophomore tight end who has spent most of the 2026 campaign coping with injury. 
 The fourth Texas player who will not suit up on Saturday is talented freshman edge rusher Richard Wesley . Steve Sarkisian indicated two weeks ago that the Longhorns hope to get Wesley back at some point this season. 
 Not named on the list are wide receiver Cam Coleman and edge rusher Colin Simmons . Coleman, who has 409 receiving yards and seven touchdowns on the season, did not play last week against Missouri. He was questionable all week and was considered a game-time decision on Saturday after leaving the win over Mississippi State with an injury. 
 Simmons, who leads the Power Four in sacks and tackles for loss, has been coping with an injured ankle since a loss to Florida on Oct. 17. He missed two games, then played 18 snaps last week against Mizzou. He left the game at halftime and was seen walking the sideline without his cleats. 
 The absence of both players from the report — as well as starting defensive backs Graceson Littleton and Kade Phillips — indicates that they're set to play this week, but it remains to be seen if they're healthy enough to be as effective as usual. 
 The Longhorns and Tigers are scheduled to kick off at 6:30 p.m. from Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge on Saturday. The SEC released a statement on Friday that said it would "monitor developments and work with our institutions to determine whether any adjustments to scheduled competitions become necessary" in the wake of the air travel disruption on Friday.
